summary: Add two exact minimum-side advances: a general-n dual-event determinant-parity calibration and uniform compact finite-contrast reflection or nonexistence strips near mu=2. Record the remaining det(H)>0 obligation and bounded failed routes without changing the open global target.

node.title: Dual event Schur parity calibrates the minimum continuant orientation
node.statement: The accepted physical minimum relative-continuant representation and alternating event allocation, followed by two exact Sylvester determinant identities, imply the determinant-parity equivalence stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DETERMINANT-PARITY-R35.

node.title: Minimum dual-event determinant parity
node.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse common-terminal minimum-law root with 2n events, let L_- be the accepted (2n-1)-dimensional relative path matrix. Split the n positive odd edges and n-1 negative even edges in the dual event matrix M=P-C^T W^(-1)C, with P>0 and W>0, and put H=C P^(-1)C^T-W. Then sign det(L_-)=sign det(H), including the zero-determinant case. Hence the exact R7 minimum orientation requirement is det(H)>0. For n=2 this agrees with H>0; for n>=3 it is algebraically strictly weaker than positive definiteness. The claim does not prove det(H)>0, root order, reflection symmetry, uniqueness, or existence.

node.title: Properness transports the mu=2 minimum anchor to a compact spectral strip
node.statement: Finite-contrast properness and relay-coordinate continuity, combined with local implicit uniqueness at reflection-fixed anchor roots, prove a compact anchor-slice lemma. Applying the trusted n=2 mu=2 twist and global order and the trusted n>=3 mu=2 nonexistence theorem gives the two strip conclusions in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-COMPACT-MU2-STRIP-R35.

node.title: Compact finite-contrast minimum reflection and exclusion strips near mu=2
node.statement: Fix a compact finite-contrast interval K=[1+eta,M] with eta>0 and M<infinity. There is delta_2(K)>0 such that every premise-complete min-self-consistent four-switch point with R in K and |mu-2|<delta_2(K) is reflection invariant. For every fixed integer n>=3 there is delta_n(K)>0 such that no premise-complete min-self-consistent 2n-switch point with R in K has |mu-2|<delta_n(K). More generally, for any fixed n, fixed relay sign, and anchor mu_0>1 on such a compact K, reflection fixing plus nonzero partial_q A_n at every anchor root yields a uniform reflection-only neighborhood, while an empty anchor slice yields a uniform empty neighborhood. The widths need not be effective or uniform in n, and no statement is made for arbitrary mu, R down to 1, or unbounded R.

node.title: Orient the minimum dual-event determinant
node.statement: Prove det(H)>0 for every physical premise-complete event-transverse minimum-law common-terminal root, or produce an exact or rigorously certified violating root.
node.formal_statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, mu>1, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse minimum-law common-terminal root, form the physical dual negative-edge Schur matrix H=C P^(-1)C^T-W from CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DETERMINANT-PARITY-R35. Prove det(H)>0; equivalently prove det(L_-)>0, J<0, and partial_q A_n<0. Alternatively certify a fully physical root with det(H)<=0.
discharge_criteria: Cover every finite R>1, n>=2, and mu>1, every relay chamber and compatible closure, and arbitrary asymmetric common-terminal roots.
Prove determinant positivity itself; do not replace it by the unnecessarily stronger H>0 or complementary-inertia assertion for n>=3.
Retain the relative scaling quotient and every event saltation coefficient, endpoint cell, parity, terminal soft-pair limit, and possible q-Jacobi singular root.

A counterexample must satisfy the complete physical relay, common-terminal, event-count, sign-law, phase, transversality, and energy predicates; relaxed matrices, local interfaces, and finite floating searches do not discharge the obligation.

If determinant orientation is proved, invoke the accepted global chamber/closure bridge separately; do not infer full equal-norm uniqueness or the stronger canonical minimum claim from the local lemma alone.

node.title: Minimum-side global reflection program after determinant calibration
node.statement: The run proves compact mu=2 reflection or exclusion strips and calibrates the general-n local event target from H>0 to the strictly weaker det(H)>0. It also derives an exact ordered-involution/endpoint-norming reduction, extends finite n=2 interface coverage on bounded parameter faces, and performs a frozen numerical search that finds no asymmetric or singular candidate. Arbitrary-mu all-n reflection remains open at either the physical determinant sign or a direct cross-root endpoint-order bridge; incomplete finite certificates and null searches are non-propagating.
node.method_family: Reflection involutions, terminal norming order, proper compact anchor continuation, event-matrix determinant parity, normalized boundary asymptotics, directed interval arithmetic, and deterministic falsification
node.deliverable_contract: A proof or refutation of reflection fixing for every finite-contrast minimum-law self-consistent exact-2n-switch point, with exact weaker lemmas integrated and every uncovered frequency, contrast, event boundary, and disconnected component explicit.
falsification_tests: Keep arbitrary asymmetric roots until reflection fixing is proved; do not work only in the symmetric ansatz.
Audit n=2 at arbitrary mu, n>=3, mu down to 1, large mu, both endpoint norming factors, and reflection two-cycles.
Do not infer all-root symmetry from properness, degree, or a surviving symmetric branch; an exact pitchfork model refutes that mechanism.
Do not promote finite binary64 or high-precision null searches, single-face interval certificates, or relaxed algebraic witnesses to a universal theorem or counterexample.
Distinguish determinant orientation from positive definiteness for n>=3 and retain the permanent scaling quotient correctly.
node.expected_bottleneck: The general-n physical dual determinant is unsigned. A mechanism-distinct direct route also lacks any accepted identity comparing endpoint norming data across two distinct equal-integral minimum roots; one-root action identities leave the alternating endpoint defect uncontrolled.

rationale.scope: The determinant lemma covers every finite R>1 and n>=2 but only calibrates the missing local sign. The strip theorem is uniform only on one compact finite-contrast interval for fixed n near mu=2. Arbitrary mu, noncompact contrast limits, and the universal reflection theorem remain open.
rationale.duplicate_policy: R7 identifies det(L_-) as the orientation target but does not relate it to the general-n dual negative-edge determinant. R10 gives H>0 only for n=2,mu=2. R10/R11/R15 give exact mu=2 slices but not a uniform compact neighborhood. The new det(H)>0 obligation is explicitly a minimum-only specialization and Schur reformulation of the existing all-sign R7 continuant obligation; it is also weaker than the existing minimum complementary-inertia obligation.
rationale.computation_policy: No numerical search or finite interval face certificate is a theorem premise. Those artifacts are attached only to the partial attempt and remain explicitly non-propagating because their R14/R17 analytic upstream is not canonical.
rationale.audit_policy: The determinant proof is bound to sha256:2e4619ac52392aadf00369e8c9afdea3ddf76ec5e3d00452dc44a258ee8de40b; the compact strip proof is bound to sha256:2eacbd9e31b85e21180479ac70165f1e369381835334aa5204a83958fc2b763f. Independent proposal review is required before integration.

ordered_steps: Use the accepted R7 coefficients a_i>0. The explicit physical formula for K_i has a positive sine numerator by the trusted internal-phase range, while the trusted alternating event/nodal allocation gives sign(U_i U_(i+1))=(-1)^(i+1); hence sign(K_i)=(-1)^(i+1) and L_-=K+B D^(-1)B^T.
Define M=D+B^T K^(-1)B. Sylvester's determinant identity gives det(M)={det(D)/det(K)}det(L_-); exactly n-1 entries of K are negative.
Partition B into positive odd rows and negative even rows to obtain M=P-C^T W^(-1)C with P>0 and W>0, and define H=C P^(-1)C^T-W.
A second Sylvester/Schur determinant identity gives det(M)=(-1)^(n-1){det(P)/det(W)}det(H). Comparing both signed identities yields sign det(L_-)=sign det(H), including zero.
Apply the accepted R7 bridge to identify det(H)>0 as exactly equivalent to det(L_-)>0, J<0, and partial_q A_n<0; do not infer the still-open sign itself.
boundary_cases: The first case n=2 has dim(H)=1, while n>=3 permits mixed inertia with positive determinant; the proof never substitutes positive definiteness for determinant orientation.
The permanent scaling Jacobi field is not counted because the accepted R7 matrix is already in relative coordinates.
All K_i are nonzero only in the premise-complete event-transverse physical scope; this does not assume partial_q A_n!=0. Grazing, collisions, incomplete words, and R=1 are excluded.
The result is conditional on a physical common-terminal root and asserts neither root existence, determinant positivity, reflection symmetry, nor global uniqueness.

ordered_steps: Assume a sequence of asymmetric self-consistent roots over compact K has mu converging to an anchor mu0. Trusted properness extracts an interior self-consistent limit on the anchor slice, and relay coordinates including q converge.

If every anchor root is reflection fixed and partial_q A_n is nonzero, the implicit-function theorem gives at most one nearby common-terminal q root for each nearby (R,mu), including a relative R>1 neighborhood at an endpoint of K.

By the trusted symplectic reflection claim, each asymmetric root and its reflection have the same (R,mu), distinct q coordinates because q^sharp=q is equivalent to reflection fixing, and both converge to the fixed anchor q, contradicting local uniqueness. If the anchor slice is empty, compactness alone contradicts the sequence.
For n=2 and mu0=2, trusted R11 fixes every anchor root and trusted R10 supplies partial_q A_2<0, so the compact reflection strip follows.
For each fixed n>=3 and mu0=2, trusted R15 makes the entire common-terminal anchor slice empty, so the compact empty strip follows.
boundary_cases: The n=2 conclusion is conditional on roots and may be vacuous for some parameters; the n>=3 conclusion is genuine nonexistence in the stated compact strip.

The limit stays in the same exact-2n-switch, event-transverse, minimum self-consistency class because properness gives a uniform positive lower bound on all 2n+1 cell lengths and full-relay coordinates are continuous; no q-Jacobi nonsingularity is assumed except at the n=2 anchor where R10 supplies it.
The widths may depend on n, eta, and M; no effective bound, uniform-in-n statement, R down to 1 limit, or unbounded-contrast conclusion is claimed.
A disconnected asymmetric component is covered because the proof uses a contradiction sequence rather than continuation from the small-contrast branch.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: The parity equivalence is proved, but no accepted all-n argument signs the dual determinant on every physical minimum root. Existing exact and interval work covers only restricted n=2 domains.

Two exact reusable advances are proved and proposed separately. The event, asymptotic, topological, endpoint-order, and numerical routes leave explicit uncovered domains and do not settle or refute the universal target.
